key_insight: Introduce a Smooth Verifiable Reward that turns discrete, verifiable 3D physical constraints into dense, continuous supervision—eliminating near-miss suppression from relative ranking and thereby activating spatial/numeric reasoning in Vision–Language Models.
problem_solved: VLMs struggle to produce precise numerical predictions for 3D scene understanding because standard RL-based ranking rewards are sparse, unstable, and discard informative near-miss examples; the paper addresses how to exploit verifiable 3D constraints to provide stable, informative learning signals.
method: Design a Smooth Verifiable Reward (SVR) that maps verifiable 3D constraint violations into a continuous, differentiable reward signal rather than a binary/relative rank.

Integrate SVR into the RL training loop (replacing or adapting relative normalization in GRPO-style pipelines) to preserve gradient information from near-miss samples and reduce reward sparsity/instability.
Use physics- and geometry-based verifiers to generate reliable supervision from 3D scene constraints, providing dense corrective feedback for VLMs' numeric/spatial outputs.
impact: Provides a practical way to teach VLMs precise spatial and numerical reasoning with stable gradients, improving accuracy on 3D understanding and enabling stronger performance in robotics, AR, and other real-world tasks that require verifiable geometry.
visual_elements: Before/after reward diagram: sparse binary or relative reward vs. smooth continuous SVR curve showing preserved gradient around near-miss samples
Pipeline flowchart: input image+text → verifiable 3D constraint checker → SVR computation → RL update (highlighting change from relative normalization)
Performance bar/line chart: accuracy or error on 3D numeric tasks comparing baseline RL, ranking methods, and SVR
Illustrated 3D scene with predicted vs. ground-truth numeric measurements to show reduced error and better spatial alignment
paper_title: Smooth Operator: Smooth Verifiable Reward Activates Spatial Reasoning Ability of Vision-Language Model
paper_authors: Siwen Jiao, Tianxiong Lv, Kangan Qian, Chenxu Zhao, Xiuyuan Zhu
